findings.reason: an author shown compile_host_memory.py would either extend it — it already measures the same weak-row solve program's host memory and executable size — or state in writing why a second parent/child harness is required, and either answer shrinks the plan.
findings.text: the plan's §1 sampler and §2 one-row-per-process remedy re-derive "fresh child process per program, parent drives the children, persist a part receipt per landing" while the repository already ships that exact shape for a compile-rung sweep, and the plan cites neither it nor scripts/h200_test_lane/prewarm_row.py, whose module docstring states each program is issued in its own process because "a sequence run in one process exhausts the LLVM section allocator" — the very failure this plan exists to route around

findings.reason: the recognition has to live where the run's outcome is recorded, not inside a pytest session plugin, so the plan's §3 site must move before the node is released.
findings.text: §3 names cache_guard, a plugin whose only entry points are pytest_sessionstart and pytest_sessionfinish, as the place to say "it is a compile abort, at the moment it happens", but the aborting runs are CPU debug allocations that drive benchmarks/solve_program_size_gate.py outside pytest and are killed by SIGABRT before any session hook returns, so the interface §3 proposes to add a classifier to is never entered on the failure it is meant to name

findings.reason: a duplicate classifier beside run.sh's own outcome records drifts from it, and naming the owner (run.sh for the job log, compile_abort_probe.py for the signature) tells the author which file to extend instead of forking.
findings.text: the plan re-implements the job-outcome diagnostic in a second place rather than extending the mechanism that already owns it: scripts/nova_lane/run.sh prints named outcome diagnostics into the log (SOURCE_REVISION_MISMATCH at :221, SLURM_JOB_ID/RUNG/EXIT_STATUS in wait_for_job at :378) and reads the scheduler's ExitCode, which is exactly the "scheduler reports the step as ended rather than as failed" seam §3 describes, while benchmarks/compile_abort_probe.py already carries the section-memory vocabulary and the mapping evidence

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §1's benchmarks/compile_abort_probe.py is one module hiding the /proc sampling, the liveness rule, persist-as-you-sample and the summary behind a single main(), and §3's classifier is a small honest function rather than a spread of wrappers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the remedy and receipt machinery the plan adds forks the parent-drives-sequential-subprocesses + persist-a-part-receipt-per-landing behaviour already owned by benchmarks/compile_host_memory.py and scripts/h200_test_lane/prewarm_row.py, rather than extending one of them.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan builds a parent/child sampler for §1 and a per-row process isolator for §2 without citing benchmarks/compile_host_memory.py, which already drives each compile rung in a fresh child process and persists a part receipt as each one lands, the same two properties.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §3 adds a thin recognition layer onto scripts/h200_test_lane/cache_guard.py without saying why the machinery that already owns the section-memory vocabulary (benchmarks/compile_abort_probe.py) or the job-outcome record (scripts/nova_lane/run.sh) cannot carry the classification instead.
